# Draft:Battle of Diyala (1822) 1

The Battle of Diyala (1822) was a military engagement that took place in the Diyala region in northeastern Iraq during the Qajar campaign against Baghdad. It was fought between the Shammar tribe, led by Sheikh Safuq al-Jarba, and the Qajar Empire under the command of Mohammad Mirza.
The battle began after the Qajar forces attempted to besiege Baghdad and advanced toward Diyala. In response, the Ottoman governor, Dawud Pasha, dispatched Sheikh Safuq al-Jarba and the Shammar tribe to repel the Qajar invasion. Safuq prepared a well-planned ambush involving approximately 800 cavalrymen, who succeeded in inflicting a decisive defeat on the Qajar forces after fierce fighting. The battle ended with a crushing victory for the Shammar tribe and the retreat of the Qajar forces back into Iranian territory.

Safuq al-Jarba’s plan was to lure the Qajar forces and the Shammar tribe across the Diyala River. Safuq al-Jarba and his tribesmen crossed first, and the Qajar troops followed them over the bridge. Once the Qajars had crossed, the Shammar cavalry suddenly turned back against them, charging into their ranks and engaging them at close quarters. Fierce fighting erupted, with warriors shouting amid the clash of arms. Within a short time, the Qajar army began to collapse due to the narrowness of the bridge, which made their retreat extremely difficult. The troops crowded in an attempt to withdraw, and it was there that a massacre was inflicted upon the Qajar forces.
